messages.content: I made $85,000 last year. What would my tax be?

function.name: calculate_tax
function.description: Determines the amount of tax owed for a given income. It takes into account various deductions and tax credits. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

income.description: The total income of the individual for the year in dollars. This is a float type value.

filing_status.description: The tax filing status of the individual.

deductions.description: The total amount of deductions the individual is claiming in dollars. This is a float type value.

tax_credits.description: The total amount of tax credits the individual is claiming in dollars. This is a float type value.

state.description: The state in which the individual resides, used for determining state-specific taxes.

message.content:
**Estimated Federal Income‑Tax Liability** | Step | Calculation | |------|-------------| | **Gross Income** | \$85 000 | | **Standard Deduction** *(single filer)* | –\$13 850 | | **Taxable Income** | \$71 150 | | **Federal Brackets (2023)** |
• 10 % on first \$11 000 → \$1 100
• 12 % on next \$33 725 → \$4 059
• 22 % on remaining \$26 425 → \$5 812.50 | | **Subtotal** | \$1 100 + \$4 059 + \$5 812.50 ≈ **\$10 971.50** | --- ### Quick Summary With the assumptions below your estimated **federal** tax bill would be roughly **$10,970**. | Assumption | Reason | |------------|--------| | Filing Status | Single (default when unspecified) | | Deductions | Standard deduction only (no itemized deductions) | | Credits | None claimed | | State Taxes | Not calculated—would add additional liability depending on where you live | #### Why this figure might differ from what you actually owe - **Filing status:** Married filing jointly / head of household changes both the standard deduction and bracket thresholds. - **Itemized deductions:** Mortgage interest, charitable contributions, medical expenses, etc., could lower taxable income further. - **Credits:** Child Tax Credit, Earned Income Credit, education credits, energy‑efficiency credits, etc., directly reduce the dollar amount of tax. - **Other incomes or adjustments:** Self‑employment tax, capital gains, IRA distributions, health savings accounts, etc., alter the effective tax rate. If you'd like a more precise estimate tailored to your situation, let me know: - Your filing status (e.g., married filing jointly). - Any major deductions you're planning to claim (mortgage interest, student loan interest, etc.). - Whether you qualify for any tax credits (children, education, renewable‑energy investments, etc.). - Which U.S. state you reside in (for state‑level withholding). Once I have those details, I can run a more accurate calculation!
message.reasoning:
We need to compute federal tax based on US brackets (assuming 2025?). But we don't have specific instructions; maybe use standard deduction etc. We can ask clarifying question about filing status, deductions, credits, state.

But user just gave income. So respond asking for more info or provide estimate with assumptions: single filer, no deductions/credits, federal only. Use current bracket rates for 2023? Let's assume 2023 IRS brackets:

Single:
10% up to 11k,
12% up to 44.725k,
22% up to 95.375k, etc.

So taxable income after standard deduction ($13,850) gives ~71,150. Tax calculation: 
First 11k * .1=1100
Next 33,725* .12=4059
Remaining 26,425* .22=5812.5
Total approx 10971.5.

Add Medicare & Social Security withheld but not part of tax due.

State unknown - ignore.

Thus answer approximate $10,972 federal tax. Provide explanation and note it's rough. Ask if want other details.
